!Series_title	"Alteration of peripheral blood monocyte gene expression in humans following diesel exhaust inhalation"
!Series_geo_accession	"GSE25531"
!Series_status	"Public on Nov 17 2013"
!Series_submission_date	"Nov 22 2010"
!Series_last_update_date	"Jan 23 2019"
!Series_summary	"Background: Epidemiologic associations between acutely increased cardiorespiratory morbidity and mortality and particulate air pollution are well-established, but the effects of acute pollution exposure on human gene expression changes are not well understood."
!Series_summary	""
!Series_summary	"Objectives: In order to identify potential mechanisms underlying epidemiologic associations between air pollution and morbidity, we explored changes in gene expression in humans following inhalation of fresh diesel exhaust (DE), a model for particulate air pollution."
!Series_summary	""
!Series_summary	"Methods: 14 ethnically homogeneous (white males), young, healthy subjects underwent sixty minute inhalation exposures on 2 separate days with clean air (CA) or freshly generated and diluted DE at a concentration of 300 μg/m3 PM2.5. Prior to and 24 hours following each session, whole blood was sampled and fractionated for PBMC isolation, RNA extraction, and generation of cDNA, followed by hybridization with Agilent Whole Human Genome (4X44K) arrays."
!Series_summary	""
!Series_summary	"Results: Oxidative stress and the ubiquitin proteasome pathway, as well as the coagulation system, were among hypothesized pathways identified by analysis of differentially expressed genes. Nine genes from these pathways were validated using real-time PCR comparing fold change in expression between DE exposed and clean (CA) days. Quantitative gene fold changes generated by real-time PCR were consistent with the directional fold changes from the microarray analysis."
!Series_summary	""
!Series_summary	"Conclusions: Changes in gene expression connected with key oxidative stress, protein degradation, and coagulation pathways are likely to underlie observed physiologic and clinical outcomes and suggest specific avenues and sensitive time points for further physiologic exploration."
!Series_overall_design	"Diesel exhaust inhalation exposure-induced human gene expression changes were measured in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. 14 white males subjects were seated in a controlled environment facility for 2 separate 60 minute inhalation exposures which occurred at least 1 week apart to either clean air and freshly generate or diluted diesel exhaust (300ug/m3 PM2.5) .Blood collection occurred immediately prior to and 24 hours following exposures. Two microarrays per subject were completed using Agilent Whole Human Genome (4X44K) arrays. Genes that were of interest to our research group were verified using Real Time PCR analysis."
!Series_type	"Expression profiling by array"
!Series_contributor	"Ashley,P,Pettit"
!Series_contributor	"Howard,M,Kipen"

!Sample_treatment_protocol_ch1	"Each exposure session lasted 60 minutes and occurred at approximately the same time of day in the early morning. Research technicians verified adherence to health, medication and dietary criteria. An ECG was recorded; blood was drawn for physiologic endpoints (to be reported elsewhere) and RNA extraction. ECG leads were attached for continuous monitoring during exposure. Following check-in and pre-exposure testing, subjects walked approximately 40 yards and took a two story elevator ride to the CEF located in the same building. Participants were confortably seated and asked to read or study during sessions. Subjects and real-time exposure data were continuously monitored by staff." !Sample_extract_protocol_ch1	"PBMC layer were collected using CPT tubes. 2ml PBMC was lysed in 6ml of Trizol LS. Add 4ml of lysed samples to a 15ml PCG tube. Add 1000ul of chroroform, close cape securely and shake vigorously by hand for 15 seconds. Then incubate on bench for 2-3 minutes. Spin samples at 3000 g at 4 degree for 15 minutes. Carefully remove the upper colourless aqueous layer to the final drop and place into a fresh tube. Add 0.75 times the volume with 100% ethanol to the aqueous phase and mix the tube gently by inversion. Pipette 700 ul of the mixture into the RNA binding column (Qiagen mini RNAeasy column). Centrifuge the column at 8000g for 15 seconds. Discard the flow through. Repeat this step until all of the aqueous phas/ethanol mixture has been trhough the column. Washing the column with 500 ul PRE buffer. Spin for 15 seconds at 8000g, discard the flow through. Wash the column again with 500ul of RPE buffer. Spin for 2 mins at 8000g and discard the flow through. To elute add 30ul nucelase free water to the center of the colunm, spin for 1 min at 8000g, dicard the column. remove 1ul for nanodrop and 1.5ul for bioanalyzer." Centrifuge the column at 8000g for 15 seconds. Discard the flow through. Repeat this step until all of the aqueous phas/ethanol mixture has been trhough the column. Washing the column with 500 ul PRE buffer. Spin for 15 seconds at 8000g, discard the flow through. Wash the column again with 500ul of RPE buffer. Spin for 2 mins at 8000g and discard the flow through. To elute add 30ul nucelase free water to the center of the colunm, spin for 1 min at 8000g, dicard the column. remove 1ul for nanodrop and 1.5ul for bioanalyzer." !Sample_hyb_protocol	"1.65 ug of Cy3-labelled cDNA was fragmented at 37°C for 30 minutes in a reaction volume of 20ul containing 2ul of Fragmentation Buffer and 1.5ul Fragmentation Enzyme following the manufacturers instructions. On completion of the fragmentation reaction, 55ul of Agilent 2X hybridization buffer and 11ul of Agilent 10X Blocking Agent and 34 ul of NuGEN Blocking reagent was added to 10ul of fragmented Cy3 labeled cDNA. The target was hybridized to Agilent Whole Human Genome Oligo Microarrays (G4112A) for 40 hours at 65 °C in a rotating Agilent hybridization oven. After hybridization, microarrays were washed 1 minute at room temperature with GE Wash Buffer 1 (Agilent) and 1 minute with 37 °C GE Wash buffer 2 (Agilent), then dried immediately by brief centrifugation."
